keyTakeaways.0: Bleap (8/10) is the top-rated stablecoin card: self-custody, 0% FX, no annual fee, EEA and UK only.

faqs.0.question: What is the best stablecoin card in 2026?
faqs.0.answer: Bleap is RItuel's top-rated stablecoin card in 2026 with a score of 8/10. It is self-custody, charges no FX, annual or top-up fees, and pays 1% cashback in USDC, but it is only available in the EEA and UK.
faqs.1.question: Which stablecoin card works in the most countries?
faqs.1.answer: Of the ten cards ranked here, Lava Private (220+ countries and territories), Plasma One (150+ countries) and MEXC Card (147 countries) have the widest availability. Always check your own country on the card page before applying.
faqs.2.question: Do stablecoin cards charge FX fees?
faqs.2.answer: Seven of the ten cards in this ranking charge 0% FX. Plasma One, Tria and SolidYield charge 1–1.5%, which matters if you spend in a currency other than the card's base currency.
faqs.3.question: What is the difference between a self-custody and a custodial stablecoin card?
faqs.3.answer: With a self-custody card, your USDC or USDT stays in a wallet you control until the moment you pay. With a custodial card, the issuer holds your stablecoins, which is simpler to use but adds counterparty risk.
body.k0: Stablecoin cards let you spend USDC or USDT like cash, without a market move changing what your balance can buy. In 2026 almost every crypto card accepts stablecoins, so the real differences are in FX fees, how cashback is paid, who holds your funds, and where you can sign up.

body.k80: How do you choose a stablecoin card?
body.geo2: Pick the card that is issued in your country first, then decide whether you want self-custody or a custodial account. After that, compare the FX fee and annual fee against the cashback you can realistically earn without staking a token. For most travellers, a 0% FX card beats a higher headline cashback rate.
body.k84: <0>Start with availability. </0>A high cashback rate is no use if the card isn't issued where you live. Check the country list first.
body.k87: <0>Decide on custody. </0>With a self-custody card, your stablecoins stay in your own wallet until you spend. With a custodial card, the issuer holds them, which is simpler but carries counterparty risk.
body.k8a: <0>Look past the headline cashback. </0>The top rate usually needs a token stake or a paid plan, and rewards paid in a volatile token can lose value.
body.k8d: <0>Watch the FX fee if you travel. </0>A 1–1.5% FX fee often costs more than a modest cashback rate earns.
